title: How Much Taylor Swift Will Owe Under Mamdani Pied-à-Terre Tax
summary:
Your tax bill's waiting for you — and music superstar Taylor Swift no longer has a blank space on what she owes the city.
Newly updated Department of Finance documents show how much wealthy second-home owners in the city are being asked to pay come January 1.
Based on those documents, Swift's new pied-à-terre tax bill for her part-time homes in New York will add up to just over $133,000.
New York City's pied-à-terre tax, which is estimated to raise more than $500 million, got a green light from state lawmakers in May after years of proposals.
The amount raised by the tax could fund some of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's priorities.

title: Are American Voters Actually Gloomy About the Economy, or Is Something Else Going On?
summary:
This debate matters politically because voters are placing an overwhelming priority on the economy as an issue in the midterms.
Meanwhile, the overall drop in voters’ economic outlook has largely been driven by growing pessimism among Republicans.
Inflation-adjusted wages actually increased between 2022 and the first half of 2026, all while consumer sentiment remained weak.
In short, Americans’ economic malaise might be driven by concerns over income and wealth that conventional measures don’t fully capture.
If consumer sentiment follows a similar path, that could explain the divergence between generally strong economic trends and weak consumer sentiment.

title: Job ghosting: What applicants can do if employers do not respond
summary:
Have you ever applied for a job or attended an interview, only to hear absolutely nothing back from the employer?
So-called "job ghosting" has become a big problem for jobseekers in the UK, leaving them "demoralised", denting their confidence and undermining their hopes of finding work.
